en.title: Merge All Intersecting Closed Intervals
en.description:
Given several closed intervals [start,end], merge all intervals that overlap each other or are linked through a chain of overlaps, and return the non-overlapping covering intervals in increasing order of start. Sharing an endpoint also counts as overlapping.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n, followed by n lines each containing start end. The raw constraints themselves are cut off at 1<; this site specifies 1≤n≤200000, −10^9≤start≤end≤10^9.
en.output: The first line contains the number of merged intervals m, followed by m lines each containing start end, in increasing order of start.
en.explanation: The results are 3 intervals [1,6],[8,10],[15,18]; 1 interval [1,5]; and 2 intervals [2,2],[3,4]. Adjacent integers do not intersect.
hints: Sort by start. If the next start is ≤ the current end, extend the current end to the larger of the two; otherwise output the current interval and start a new one.
